The main takeaway from our work is that

the S. japonicum genome is much more complex and diverse than previously anticipated and is characterized by a large number of genes with putative functions in host-parasite interactions and immune evasion.

the SjDB is the first comprehensive protein database for S. japonicum that can be used to identify proteins from the various developmental stages of the parasite and tissues at the schistosome-mammalian host interface, and it will be a valuable resource for the schistosome research community.
